Verde Wilds.title: Closed Canopy
Verde Wilds.description: Dense equatorial vegetation surrounds Greenwood's isolated scientific outposts and river crossings. The closed canopy excludes Aerial profiles and limits visibility at every elevation, favouring fighting within 24 inches. Local knowledge briefly opens a longer sightline for the controlling force.
Verde Wilds.effect:
Profiles with Aerial cannot be included.

Line of Sight is limited to 24 inches, regardless of elevation. Skills and attacks that do not require Line of Sight work normally.
Verde Wilds.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Verde Wilds.owner: Once per game, one friendly trooper may draw Line of Sight up to 32 inches for one Order. An enemy targeted this way receives reciprocal Line of Sight to that trooper for the Order. Terrain still blocks Line of Sight normally.

Korin Range.title: Mountain Country
Korin Range.description: Pale fractured mountains, steep research valleys and exposed high passes define Korin Range. Trails and buildings offer reliable routes through otherwise difficult ground. Mountain-trained troops retain their mobility, while the territory's restrictions keep TAGs out of these battles.
Korin Range.effect:
All terrain is Mountain Difficult Terrain, except agreed trails, clearings and buildings.

TAGs cannot be included.
Korin Range.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Korin Range.owner: Before deployment, choose three friendly troopers. They gain Terrain (Mountain) for the game.

Crystal Frontier.title: Electromagnetic Interference
Crystal Frontier.description: Quarry terraces, quartz ravines and mineral research stations sit amid fractured crystal deposits. Electromagnetic interference disrupts remote hacking relays, forcing Hackers to operate within their own Hacking Areas. Local shielding offers the controlling faction one chance to resist an electronic attack.
Crystal Frontier.effect:
Repeaters do not extend a Hacker's Hacking Area. Hackers can still use their own Hacking Area normally.

Repeaters remain on the table and may still be targeted or affected by rules that interact with them.
Crystal Frontier.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Crystal Frontier.owner: Once per game, reroll one failed Saving Roll caused by a Hacking Attack or an E/M weapon. Accept the second result.

Azure Coast.title: Tidal Channels
Azure Coast.description: Port Meridian combines modern waterfront structures, customs facilities and maritime logistics infrastructure. Water channels create sheltered approaches for troops adapted to aquatic terrain, while supply caches offer equipment to either side. The owner's corrosion protection provides one opportunity to preserve a trooper with STR.
Azure Coast.effect:
All water features are Aquatic Difficult Terrain.

A trooper with Terrain (Aquatic) or Terrain (Total) whose base is entirely inside a water feature gains Total Cover while in that area.

An observer with Terrain (Aquatic) or Terrain (Total) ignores this water-based Total Cover when drawing Line of Sight to the protected trooper.

If the protected trooper declares a Skill that would normally break Stealth, it loses this Total Cover for the rest of that Order. After the Order, protection returns if it still qualifies.

Place four Supply Caches outside the Deployment Zones. They function as Panoplies.
Azure Coast.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Azure Coast.owner: Once per game, reroll one failed Saving Roll made by a friendly trooper with STR. Accept the second result.

Echo Shores.title: Black-Market Arsenal
Echo Shores.description: Freeport Echo is a rough coastal trading zone of working docks, cargo warehouses and improvised market streets. Smugglers and unofficial suppliers keep equipment moving through both the waterfront and the crowded bazaar. Irregular troops can draw on those stocks, and established scavengers have a better chance of finding useful gear.
Echo Shores.effect:
All troopers with the Irregular characteristic gain Booty.

Troopers that already have Booty may reroll their Booty result once, accepting the second result.

Normal army-building restrictions remain unchanged.
Echo Shores.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Echo Shores.owner: Once per game, the owner may reroll one friendly trooper's Booty result. This may be used after the battlefield-rule reroll. The new result stands.

Harmony Province.title: Security Surveillance
Harmony Province.description: Planned civic plazas, government buildings and O-12 security facilities make Harmony Province a closely watched battlefield. Surveillance prevents troops from using Camouflaged State and assists Discover attempts. Control of the local intelligence network gives the owner a second chance at a mission objective.
Harmony Province.effect:
All Discover Rolls receive +3 WIP.

Troopers cannot deploy in or enter Camouflaged State. Profiles with Camouflage may be included and deploy as models.

Impersonation and Hidden Deployment work normally.
Harmony Province.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Harmony Province.owner: Once per game, reroll one failed WIP Roll to accomplish a mission objective. Accept the second result.

Ember Highlands.title: Volcanic Updrafts
Ember Highlands.description: Dark red mesas, narrow canyon routes and geothermal installations mark this volcanic frontier. Unstable updrafts prevent the use of Super-Jump, including Jet Propulsion variants, while ordinary Jump remains available. The controlling force can exploit one carefully chosen jump to cross the broken landscape more efficiently.
Ember Highlands.effect:
Troopers cannot use Super-Jump, including Super-Jump (Jet Propulsion).

Ordinary Jump works normally.
Ember Highlands.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Ember Highlands.owner: Once per game, one friendly trooper may declare ordinary Jump as a Short Movement Skill instead of an Entire Order. Declare this before its first Skill. All other ordinary Jump restrictions apply.

Sulfur Basin.title: Toxic Fumes
Sulfur Basin.description: Refineries, tanks and extraction machinery stand across chemically scarred ground. Toxic exposure makes movement outside buildings hazardous. Resistant troopers protect their Fireteams, and local protective supplies let the controlling faction give one trooper Terrain (Total) for the scenario.
Sulfur Basin.effect:
All areas outside buildings are Toxic Zones. Agree which areas count as building interiors before deployment.

Once per Order, a trooper whose base enters or moves within a Toxic Zone makes one ARM Saving Roll against PS 10 at the end of that Order. This applies in both Active and Reactive turns.

A failed Saving Roll causes 1 Wound or STR damage, as appropriate. Remaining stationary does not trigger a roll.

Troopers with Immunity (ARM), Immunity (Enhanced), Immunity (BTS), Immunity (Continuous Damage) or Terrain (Total) ignore this territory rule.

This protection also extends to every trooper in a Fireteam containing a trooper with any of those skills.
Sulfur Basin.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Sulfur Basin.owner: At the beginning of the scenario, choose one friendly trooper. It gains Terrain (Total) for the scenario. This also protects every trooper in its Fireteam from Toxic Fumes.

Frostreach Wastes.title: Drifting Snowstorms
Frostreach Wastes.description: Ice formations shelter a small polar settlement and scattered expedition sites. Drifting snowstorms shift the battlefield's difficult ground and shooting penalties as the game progresses. Local weather readings let the owner influence one storm's movement at a critical moment.
Frostreach Wastes.effect:
Before deployment, place three circular templates on the table's centerline: one at the midpoint and the others 12 inches to either side.

At the start of each Player Turn, roll a d20 separately for each storm. Move it 6 inches toward its numbered edge, keeping its orientation fixed. Remove it when its center crosses the table edge.

Storms are Difficult Terrain Zones. BS Attacks whose Line of Sight passes through a storm suffer -3, including attacks starting or ending inside one. Overlapping storms do not stack this penalty.
Frostreach Wastes.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Frostreach Wastes.owner: Once per game, after a storm's direction roll but before moving it, reroll or negate that roll. Accept a reroll; negating leaves the storm stationary for that movement.

Northward Expanse.title: Frontier Reconnaissance
Northward Expanse.description: A dry scientific frontier stretches from New Al-Medina's permanent research stations into isolated survey country. Wind-eroded ridges, rocky outcrops and shallow gullies provide approaches across the broad landscape. Light Infantry can establish forward positions, with a surveyed route giving the owner one deeper deployment.
Northward Expanse.effect: All Light Infantry (LI) gain Forward Deployment (+4 inches). This does not stack with existing Forward Deployment; use the better value.
Northward Expanse.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Northward Expanse.owner: Before deployment, choose one friendly Light Infantry trooper. It gains Forward Deployment (+8 inches) instead. Use the better value if it already has Forward Deployment; do not add the distances.

Iron Corridor.title: Reinforced Industrial Zone
Iron Corridor.description: Advanced freight yards, cargo trains and robotic maintenance facilities create a landscape of industrial cover. Reinforced positions provide greater protection, including against Template Weapons when the cover requirements are met. The controlling force can make one position especially resilient for a single Order.
Iron Corridor.effect:
Increase the ARM bonus granted by Partial Cover by 1.

Template Weapons do not ignore the ARM bonus granted by Partial Cover, including the territory's extra +1 ARM. The trooper must meet normal Partial Cover requirements against the attacker.
Iron Corridor.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Iron Corridor.owner: Once per game, before any rolls during an Order, choose one friendly trooper. Increase the ARM bonus it receives from Partial Cover by an additional +3 for the rest of that Order. It must qualify for Partial Cover against each attack.

Nova Prospect.title: Rapid Transit Network
Nova Prospect.description: Aurora VII's colonial capital connects administrative districts, communications hubs and orbital supply facilities. Its rapid transit network lets existing Parachutist units reach the fighting efficiently, while local control gives a chosen reinforcement additional operational flexibility.
Nova Prospect.effect:
Troopers that already have Parachutist may arrive without spending their own Order. They retain that Order for use after arrival; Regular and Irregular Orders retain their normal restrictions.

Arrival generates AROs and follows normal Parachutist placement restrictions, including no Partial Cover during the arrival Order. This rule does not grant Parachutist.
Nova Prospect.details: Both players use the battlefield rule. Only the controlling faction receives the owner advantage. Normal points, SWC and availability apply.
Nova Prospect.owner: Before deployment, choose one friendly trooper that already has Parachutist. It gains Tactical Awareness in addition to the rapid transit benefit. A trooper that already has Tactical Awareness receives no second Tactical Order.
